currentContext.strengths: Diversified geographic presence across India, Europe and other international markets, mitigating single-market dependence|Dual-brand strategy (Apollo Tyres + Vredestein) spanning mass, premium and luxury price points with growing global brand recognition|Comprehensive product portfolio across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, off-highway tyres and two-wheelers, positioning it as a full-range Indian tyre manufacturer|Strong distribution network across key markets enabling deep penetration and last-mile connectivity|State-of-the-art, highly automated manufacturing facilities across India and Europe supported by a robust global supply chain|Strong market position in India's commercial vehicle and passenger vehicle segments|Global, culturally diverse management team supporting execution across markets|Ongoing R&D investment via dedicated facilities in India, Netherlands and Hungary supporting product innovation|Long-standing relationships with leading global OEMs and expanding presence in premium OEM segments (e.g. BMW, Mercedes, MG, VinFast fitments)|Vredestein products consistently top-ranked by independent testing agencies and automotive media in the premium/performance segment|Brand-building via BCCI/Team India cricket sponsorship enhancing visibility and consumer connect|Early mover initiatives in electric-vehicle tyre development
currentContext.strategies: Continued focus on strengthening the premium product portfolio, expanding the distribution network and investing in brand building and R&D|Transformation initiatives aligned with the strategic roadmap, focused on driving operational efficiency, improving product mix and unlocking long-term value|Dual-brand premiumisation strategy - positioning Vredestein as a premium/luxury brand while Apollo Tyres anchors the mass-premium/OEM segments, across India, Europe and Americas|Continued expansion into North America to diversify revenue streams|Strengthening sourcing strategy through supplier collaboration, diversification and onboarding of new suppliers, plus continued sustainable procurement (ISO 20400:2017, GPSNR engagement, INROAD domestic natural-rubber sourcing)|Development of indigenised, defence-aligned commercial-vehicle tyre products under the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, and introduction of EV-specific tyre patterns across CV and other segments|Brand building via sponsorship platforms (BCCI/Team India jersey partnership, 'Har Safar Mein Dum Hai' campaign in India, 'Demand a Better Tire' campaign in the Americas)|Future outlook: continued focus on driving sustainable and profitable growth through disciplined capital allocation and cost optimisation amid an evolving global macro/geopolitical environment
currentContext.expansion: No new manufacturing plant or capacity-addition project with a commissioning/ramp timeline is disclosed in this bundle. Expansion activity described is largely commercial/footprint-led: continued distribution-network expansion and brand-building investment in India (Vredestein premiumisation), portfolio expansion in Europe into higher-value UHP/UUHP segments, and continued expansion into North America (dealer-network expansion plus the 'Demand a Better Tire' campaign) as a new avenue for revenue diversification. Product-portfolio expansion during FY26 included the Aspire 5 UHP range and enhanced Amazer 4G Life (PCR), the apterra HT5 highway-terrain tyre (CV/SUV), VIRAT range extensions and steel-breaker Tractor Rear tyres (Farm OHT), and the 16.00-25 Terra MT and Terra G3 (Industrial OHT). The Company also referenced its 'state-of-the-art facility in Andhra Pradesh' as the venue for the FY26 Global Partners' Summit, without describing any new capacity build there.
currentContext.mdna: Domestic tyre demand expected to grow 6-8% during FY26, driven by improving affordability and favourable rural demand conditions|Replacement segment growth strengthened, particularly in H2FY26, supported by GST rationalisation and improved consumption trends|OEM demand remained relatively moderate across passenger and commercial vehicle segments, while continued two-wheeler growth supported overall volumes|Rising radialisation in India's commercial vehicle segment seen as a structural growth opportunity given the Company's TBR brand equity|Passenger vehicle segment growth expected to continue on rising vehicle parc and increasing demand for premium products|Two-wheeler segment offers scale-up opportunity on growing market acceptance and favourable demand dynamics|In Europe, Vredestein's premium positioning, manufacturing footprint and increasing OEM engagements seen as levers to improve product mix and drive replacement demand|European replacement tyre market (CY25) stayed weak with volumes down across Consumer, TBR and OHT categories; rising imports into EU/UK on lower-cost competition and higher European (energy) production costs are intensifying competitive pressure|Raw material costs moderated over the first three quarters of FY26 (softer crude-based inputs) before renewed pressure in Q4 from a Brent crude spike (crossing USD 100/barrel) and continued INR depreciation, raising import costs for key inputs|Global economic outlook for CY26 expected to remain resilient, supported by steady emerging-market performance, while advanced economies see moderate growth; trade policy shifts, energy price volatility and geopolitical developments flagged as swing factors for supply chains, input costs and demand

risks.risk: Macroeconomic and demand cyclicality across key geographies
risks.note: Performance is influenced by macroeconomic conditions across geographies; any slowdown in key international markets, particularly Europe and North America, may impact demand and exports, as the tyre industry remains closely linked to overall economic activity.

Natural rubber prices are subject to agricultural factors while other key inputs (carbon black, synthetic rubber, fabric, chemicals) are influenced by crude oil price movements; these factors may impact cost structures and profitability.
Global operations and dependence on imported raw materials and export markets expose the Company to currency movements that may impact margins and earnings.

Operates in a dynamic regulatory environment with evolving norms on sustainability, emissions and safety; rapid shifts in market trends, including increasing EV adoption, require continuous adaptation in product development and business strategy.

Geopolitical developments, disruptions to global logistics, climate-related events and rising input costs may impact supply continuity and increase transportation costs in an increasingly interconnected global environment.
Intense competition from both global and domestic players requires continuous innovation, product differentiation and cost competitiveness to sustain market position.
Growing threats from cyberattacks, including ransomware and phishing attempts, may impact business continuity and data security.
Operations depend on availability of skilled manpower; challenges in talent retention, labour availability and potential labour disruptions may impact manufacturing operations and productivity.

one-line thesis: Apollo Tyres delivered record Q4 margins (14.6%) and de-leveraged to 0.4x net debt/EBITDA, but faces immediate margin compression in FY27 due to a mid-to-high teens raw material cost spike requiring multiple price hikes. The strategic closure of the Enschede plant sets the stage for European margin recovery in H2FY27, while India operations remain volume-driven despite inflationary headwinds.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 73.4B (+14% YoY); EBITDA: INR 10.7B (14.6% margin vs 13% YoY); PAT: Impacted by one-off EUR 43M non-cash write-off (Enschede) and INR 570Cr deferred tax credit (tax regime shift); Order Book: N/A (Replacement/OE flow); Net Debt/EBITDA: 0.4x (down from 3.2x in FY20). One-offs: EUR 43M asset write-down; INR 570Cr tax gain; A&P spend elevated to 4% of sales (vs normal 2%) due to cricket sponsorship.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Strong double-digit volume expected in Q1 FY27; Margin: Under pressure in Q1/Q2 FY27 due to 15-20% RM inflation, targeting recovery to 16%+ in Europe by H2 FY27; Order Inflow: April volumes strong; Capex: INR 35B for FY27 (80% India growth/expansion).
order book & pipeline: N/A for make-to-stock tyre model; Capacity utilization at 90% across India and Europe; April demand tracking Q4 levels despite price hikes.
segment / subsidiary detail: India: Revenue INR 52.4B (+14.3% YoY), EBITDA margin 14.6% (vs 11.2% YoY), volume growth high-teens in both OE and Replacement. Europe: Revenue EUR 170M (-1% YoY), EBITDA EUR 25M (14.6% margin), impacted by supply issues in TBR and muted market conditions.
growth verticals / optionality: India capacity expansion (Truck & Car) driving FY27 capex; Hungary plant passenger car expansion underway; Potential to shift more export production to India post-Enschede closure to leverage cost arbitrage.
margins & cost dynamics: Raw material basket up 1% QoQ in Q4; Current RM inflation mid-to-high teens (Natural Rubber INR 250/kg vs INR 200/kg in Q4); Price hikes of 6-8% announced for India (3-5% implemented), 2% for Europe; Further hikes needed to offset costs.
capex / expansion: INR 35B planned for FY27; ~INR 30B allocated to India (capacity expansion in TBR/PCR); Balance to Europe (Hungary PCR expansion).
capital allocation: Priority on growth capex and debt reduction; Net debt/EBITDA at 0.4x provides flexibility; EUR 50M cash outflow expected in FY27 for Enschede social plan (already provided for).
risks & watch-items: Sustained raw material inflation beyond current mid-teens; Demand destruction in H2 FY27 if price hikes accumulate; Geopolitical volatility in West Asia affecting logistics/energy; Execution risk on Enschede closure and Hungary ramp-up.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term fundamentals and balance sheet strength; Cautious on near-term margin volatility due to external cost shocks; Disciplined on capital allocation and cost control.
non-obvious takeaways: Deferred tax liability reversal of INR 570Cr due to shift to concessional tax regime (25% vs 34%) artificially boosted PAT; Europe's 'Other Operating Income' decline is non-cash amortization reversal of state aid due to asset transfer from Hungary; A&P spend spike is temporary (cricket jersey), normalizing to 2.5%.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material inflation (Natural Rubber +25% QoQ) squeezing margins for peers with weaker pricing power or higher leverage. | Apollo Tyres Ltd | beneficiary | High | Strongest balance sheet (0.4x net debt) allows absorption of short-term pain; proven ability to pass on costs (6-8% hike already); market share gains in TBR replacement; European restructuring removes structural drag by H2FY27. |

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic tyre demand expected to grow 6-8% during FY26, driven by improving affordability and favourable rural demand conditions
- Replacement segment growth strengthened, particularly in H2FY26, supported by GST rationalisation and improved consumption trends
- OEM demand remained relatively moderate across passenger and commercial vehicle segments, while continued two-wheeler growth supported overall volumes
- Rising radialisation in India's commercial vehicle segment seen as a structural growth opportunity given the Company's TBR brand equity
- Passenger vehicle segment growth expected to continue on rising vehicle parc and increasing demand for premium products
- Two-wheeler segment offers scale-up opportunity on growing market acceptance and favourable demand dynamics
- In Europe, Vredestein's premium positioning, manufacturing footprint and increasing OEM engagements seen as levers to improve product mix and drive replacement demand
- European replacement tyre market (CY25) stayed weak with volumes down across Consumer, TBR and OHT categories; rising imports into EU/UK on lower-cost competition and higher European (energy) production costs are intensifying competitive pressure
- Raw material costs moderated over the first three quarters of FY26 (softer crude-based inputs) before renewed pressure in Q4 from a Brent crude spike (crossing USD 100/barrel) and continued INR depreciation, raising import costs for key inputs
- Global economic outlook for CY26 expected to remain resilient, supported by steady emerging-market performance, while advanced economies see moderate growth; trade policy shifts, energy price volatility and geopolitical developments flagged as swing factors for supply chains, input costs and demand

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Raw material basket up 1% QoQ in Q4; Current RM inflation mid-to-high teens (Natural Rubber INR 250/kg vs INR 200/kg in Q4); Price hikes of 6-8% announced for India (3-5% implemented), 2% for Europe; Further hikes needed to offset costs.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority on growth capex and debt reduction; Net debt/EBITDA at 0.4x provides flexibility; EUR 50M cash outflow expected in FY27 for Enschede social plan (already provided for).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: No new manufacturing plant or capacity-addition project with a commissioning/ramp timeline is disclosed in this bundle. Expansion activity described is largely commercial/footprint-led: continued distribution-network expansion and brand-building investment in India (Vredestein premiumisation), portfolio expansion in Europe into higher-value UHP/UUHP segments, and continued expansion into North America (dealer-network expansion plus the 'Demand a Better Tire' campaign) as a new avenue for revenue diversification. Product-portfolio expansion during FY26 included the Aspire 5 UHP range and enhanced Amazer 4G Life (PCR), the apterra HT5 highway-terrain tyre (CV/SUV), VIRAT range extensions and steel-breaker Tractor Rear tyres (Farm OHT), and the 16.00-25 Terra MT and Terra G3 (Industrial OHT). The Company also referenced its 'state-of-the-art facility in Andhra Pradesh' as the venue for the FY26 Global Partners' Summit, without describing any new capacity build there.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term fundamentals and balance sheet strength; Cautious on near-term margin volatility due to external cost shocks; Disciplined on capital allocation and cost control.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": "true", "note": "CCI order dated 31-Aug-2018 found the Company (with other tyre manufacturers and ATMA) in contravention of Section 3 of the Competition Act, 2002, and imposed a penalty. Company appealed to NCLAT, which remanded the matter back to CCI (Dec-2022 judgement); CCI has appealed that judgement before the Supreme Court, which is pending. As on date, no penalty amount is enforceable against/payable by the Company. Disclosed under 'Significant and Material Orders Passed by Regulators' in the Board's Report.", "as_of": "2026-07-06"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified geographic presence across India, Europe and other international markets, mitigating single-market dependence
- Dual-brand strategy (Apollo Tyres + Vredestein) spanning mass, premium and luxury price points with growing global brand recognition
- Comprehensive product portfolio across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, off-highway tyres and two-wheelers, positioning it as a full-range Indian tyre manufacturer
- Strong distribution network across key markets enabling deep penetration and last-mile connectivity
- State-of-the-art, highly automated manufacturing facilities across India and Europe supported by a robust global supply chain
- Strong market position in India's commercial vehicle and passenger vehicle segments
- Global, culturally diverse management team supporting execution across markets
- Ongoing R&D investment via dedicated facilities in India, Netherlands and Hungary supporting product innovation
- Long-standing relationships with leading global OEMs and expanding presence in premium OEM segments (e.g. BMW, Mercedes, MG, VinFast fitments)
- Vredestein products consistently top-ranked by independent testing agencies and automotive media in the premium/performance segment
- Brand-building via BCCI/Team India cricket sponsorship enhancing visibility and consumer connect
- Early mover initiatives in electric-vehicle tyre development

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Sustained raw material inflation beyond current mid-teens; Demand destruction in H2 FY27 if price hikes accumulate; Geopolitical volatility in West Asia affecting logistics/energy; Execution risk on Enschede closure and Hungary ramp-up.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Deferred tax liability reversal of INR 570Cr due to shift to concessional tax regime (25% vs 34%) artificially boosted PAT; Europe's 'Other Operating Income' decline is non-cash amortization reversal of state aid due to asset transfer from Hungary; A&P spend spike is temporary (cricket jersey), normalizing to 2.5%.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continued focus on strengthening the premium product portfolio, expanding the distribution network and investing in brand building and R&D
- Transformation initiatives aligned with the strategic roadmap, focused on driving operational efficiency, improving product mix and unlocking long-term value
- Dual-brand premiumisation strategy - positioning Vredestein as a premium/luxury brand while Apollo Tyres anchors the mass-premium/OEM segments, across India, Europe and Americas
- Continued expansion into North America to diversify revenue streams
- Strengthening sourcing strategy through supplier …
